title: fix(sqlite): new work fails when idle handles fill store capacity
body:
Related: #162497

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes new SQLite work being refused when cached, idle shared-state client handles occupy all 64 broker reservations.

## User Impact

New work can reclaim owner-confirmed idle shared-state capacity without raising the cap or interrupting accepted work. Retired clients reopen on their next use; no configuration, schema, data-retention, or migration change is required. The coordinator's decision is that pressure-triggered idle-handle retirement is in scope for this bug fix.

This is a partial fix for the linked issue. Cached per-agent memory-publication workers can still retain executor borrowers, and busy or non-reclaimable clients can still exhaust capacity. The separate provider-overload classification repair is already merged in #162624.

## Why This Change Was Made

The broker previously rejected a new store as soon as 64 client handles were retained. The shared-state owner already knows how to retire idle clients and reopen them safely. Admission now asks that owner for capacity, waits for retirement, rechecks opening authority and cancellation, and reserves the freed slot synchronously. Accepted scopes, pending commands, maintenance clients, and other runtime generations remain protected. Shutdown and failed-worker cleanup remain joined.

Original fix by @PollyBot13; maintainer cleanup simplifies the context and reclamation lifetime, adds cancellation and post-retirement authority coverage, and replaces repeated native-worker test setup with in-memory contract fixtures. The shared-owner integration regression still exercises the actual 64-client limit and persisted readback.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test and typecheck gate per maintainer policy. Live Gateway proof, leases, local tests/typechecks, and production-reverted negative controls were intentionally skipped. Prior contributor runtime evidence applies to its old head, not this revision.

- Source/history: current main still rejects at `clients.size >= MAX_STORES` before checking idle ownership. The owning worker already rejects unsettled transactions/readers before command completion.
- Regression names: `reclaims only an idle shared-state client at 64 and reopens its persisted state`; `joins host drainage during reclamation without cycling through open admission`; `waits for retirement and atomically reserves the released capacity`; `refuses stale opening authority %s` (before/after retirement, cancellation, shutdown); `protects an accepted %s from idle reclamation` (scope/command); foreign-generation refusal, retirement failure, and tiny pending-open bounds.
- Local static checks: oxfmt 0.71.0 and changed-file oxlint passed (10 TypeScript files, 231 rules, no diagnostics); `git diff --check` passed. The parent install lacks the Solid UI lint dependency, so the local core configuration excludes only that unrelated UI override. No install or dependency change.
- Autoreview: local candidate and committed branch both **scoped-clean through P2**, no actionable findings. The two explicit callback return annotations correcting the first CI test-type failure also received a scoped-clean follow-up review. Main merges leave the reviewed production patch unchanged.
- Exact-head CI: [38686765003](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38686765003), head `257166fcb1a56afc0d24b3f1fa0d2795785c9cf6`, is terminal **failure with inherited infrastructure failures only**. All production/test typechecks, lint, docs, ratchets and seven selected UI jobs passed (35 successful jobs). All 22 Node test jobs failed during setup, before tests; the aggregate gate also failed. The SQLite regressions therefore remain unexecuted on this head.
- Test cost: capacity file reduced from 300 to 146 lines; one native broker shutdown case remains, alongside the existing real shared-owner integration fixture. No new timers, sleeps, or polling. The Node jobs failed before the tests started, so current regression wall time and runtime CI seconds are unavailable; no local runtime was executed.
- LOC versus merged `origin/main` (`54691736d026`): production **+121/-37 (net +84)**; tests/fixtures **+300/-35 (net +265)**; docs **+7/-0**. Positive production growth is the bounded admission/retirement plumbing; unrelated deletion is not used to meet a metric.

The latest ClawSweeper review reported no code findings. Its retention-policy question is resolved by the coordinator decision above. Additional live-proof/negative-control requests are superseded by the maintainer's PR-CI proof policy. Human reviews were absent when this revision was prepared.

Captured-fact audit: retirement carries the exact cached entry and opening runtime generation. Entry membership, idle state, maintenance ownership, active sibling operations, scopes and pending commands are checked at the retirement effect; generation identity must match. After awaited retirement, opening cancellation, live caller authority and host-drain state are checked again. Existing native admission retains its physical-path and identity checks. The closed client's captured reclamation mode describes that already-owned close and remains fixed through settlement; it grants no new access.

Remaining issue scope: `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-database-context.ts` caches a publication worker whose V2 store retains a per-agent executor borrower until close. Those intentional generation claims need a separate owner-level design before they can be reclaimed safely; simply closing them between commands could invalidate callers or cycle through recovery opens. This PR does not change that contract or claim full issue closure.

Inherited infrastructure evidence: PR [job 116263643424](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38686765003/job/116263643424) and latest scheduled main [run 38687324602 / job 116265300818](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38687324602/job/116265300818) both fail downloading `actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e`: “An action could not be found” at the same codeload archive URL. Direct archive checks returned HTTP 404. Main's matching job is terminal failure; that full scheduled run was still running at comparison time. The workflow pin is unchanged by this PR. No blind rerun or unrelated workflow change was made; runtime proof needs the infrastructure repaired.

CI correction: the first run, [38685804760](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38685804760/job/116260875228), caught TS7022/TS7023 in the new fixture's self-referencing retirement callbacks. Commit `a033e814cc75` adds explicit return types; the final head's [same type lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38686765003/job/116263905124) passes. No PR-caused CI failure remains observed. No merge performed.
